questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

The road was blocked since it was in repair.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2), i.e., In repair.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c85df1d0885ef6fd1ccb6d6eeeb4f0ac2cb3339955502df2aa31deb31b5ead58.png] ​**Explanation**:

__
 
• The error lies in option 2, which uses the incorrect preposition '**in**'.
 
• The preposition '**In**' refers to something that is surrounded by something else.*** Example: London is in England.***
 
• ** Important Point:**
 
• Here, the sentence is talking about the road being 'in the process of' being repaired.__
 
• So, the correct preposition here should be '**under**', which forms the phrase '**under repair'**. 
 
• **Under**- showing an ongoing process of something. ***Example: The house is under construction.***

​

**Thus, the rectified sentence is: ***The road was blocked since it was **under **repair. *

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Please / explain me / how this plan / did not work.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **explain me**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the segment "explain me", the correct preposition **"to"** is missing after **"explain"**. The correct phrase should be **"explain to me**".
 
• The error is related to the use of **prepositions** in English grammar.
 
• The correct construction when using the verb "explain" in the context of giving information to someone is "explain something to someone". Therefore, "explain to me" is the correct form.
 
• Without the preposition **"to",** the sentence implies a direct action on "me", which is not how the verb "explain" functions in English.

Therefore, the sentence is: *Please **explain to me** how this plan did not work.*

questions.question:
Three segments of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the option that contains the error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Since his son has not yet completed the age of eighteen, __he was reluctant to fulfil his son’s demand of getting a motorbike.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the singular form of the verb 'was' is incorrect.
 
• The correct sentence should maintain consistent tense. Since the first part of the sentence uses the present perfect tense "has not yet completed," the second part should use the present tense "**is**" instead of the past tense "**was"**.
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the verb should be 'is' instead of 'was'.

Hence, the correct statement is: ***Since his son has not yet completed the age of eighteen, he is reluctant __to fulfil his son’s demand of getting a motorbike*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When maintaining consistent tense in a sentence, **ensure **that all verbs match the initial tense used.
 
• For example, if the sentence starts in the** present perfect tense**, subsequent verbs should be in the** present tense** unless a shift in time frame is clearly indicated.

Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select "No error’.

I loved Joe - perhaps for no best reason / in those early days than / because the dear fellow let me love him.

options.text: I loved Joe - perhaps for no best reason
because the dear fellow let me love him.

questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **I loved Joe - perhaps for no best reason**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the phrase 'for no best reason' is incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be 'for no better reason', which is the **correct comparative form**.
 
• In the provided sentence, **"better"** is grammatically correct as a comparative form because it compares the speaker's reasons for loving Joe.
 
• The phrase "no better reason" implies that the speaker couldn't find any reasons that were superior or more compelling than the simple fact that Joe allowed the speaker to love him.
 
• Using "better" here sets up an implicit comparison with all other possible reasons, indicating that none of them were more valid or stronger than the reason given.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *I loved Joe - perhaps for no better reason in those early days than because the dear fellow let me love him*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Using 'best' in this context is grammatically incorrect as it implies a superlative degree, which doesn't fit the context of the sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of** "forced" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "was forced"**
 
• In the given sentence, the doer for the verb "forced" is somebody else hence, we need to use a passive voice sentence. The president hasn't left the country he was forced to do it. Hence, the doer is somebody else.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• Amazed Spiderman. (Here, the Amazed is a past participle and the doer for this is somebody else hence, we have used the past participle form)
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *The president **was forced **to leave the country when the people rose up against the government.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and click the option corresponding to it. If the sentence is free from error, click the "No error" option.**

A petty dispute between a police constable (1)/ and a motorcycle- borne couple late last night lead (2)/ to clashes between the locals and the police (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: Note that the dispute took place in the past, therefore the past form of ‘lead’ should be used in the sentence. Thus, ‘led’ should be written instead of ‘lead’ in part 2. The error lies here, hence option 2 is the correct answer.
